summary.intent: Drive the Callisto release tooling roadmap: ship refactors and fixes as stacked PRs (R5a/R5b, SYS-NAPI, R3, R1, SYS-BARRIER), prepare and verify the 0.10.3 release, then validate and research open design decisions (W3 Python partial uploads, owner contract, history bugs) before committing to them.
summary.outcome: Opened PRs #205-#209, #211, #213, #214 and #230 and resolved a stack conflict. 0.10.3 published, and research settled several W3 facts. An independent review found #230 slow and prone to misattribution; a redesign with four regression tests passed `just ci` and was pushed as a follow-up commit. The W3 decisions, derived-owner option and W10b still await the user.

repo: Characterization-first workflow works well here: add snapshot or coverage tests on current code, commit them, then do a mechanical split, and mutate the moved code to confirm the tests catch regressions.
An architecture guard forbids hand-rolled manifest parsing in callisto-graph; use `read_identity` in callisto-manifests, which accepts manifest text from a `git show` blob.
Fake-tool test harnesses hid the 0.10.1 regression; validating against real cargo/gh/git ls-remote at the release commit is a useful extra check.
The generated workflow template's jq broke when `artifactSlots` was omitted (null iteration), and the macOS test bash lacks `mapfile`, so templates need portable loops.
The CLI e2e harness has no npm fake, so dual-owner behavior can only be tested via the release simulator and executor eligibility logic.
`callisto status --format json` exposes `lastReleasedVersion`, a direct probe for tag-history ownership bugs.

Within a package, manifest order is deterministic (Cargo, npm, PyPI priority), but `select_packages` sorts through a BTreeSet, giving ecosystem-alphabetical order, so owner selection must not use `package_ids[0]`.

PyPI Warehouse returns 200 for identical-digest re-uploads and 400 for any other collision, and the simple index is cached with `max-age=600`, while the post-upload confirmation retries only about 30s.
Python builds via uv/setuptools are not byte-reproducible, even with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH for the sdist, which makes strict digest checks on rerun unsafe.
Wire-compat policy bumps a version only when a reader cannot execute the old shape; stale dual intents fail closed via ReleaseIntentStale.
A tag cache keyed by tag name rather than commit SHA caused 6000+ git subprocess calls in the history fallback.

code.finding: add_artifact_uploads loops per identity, so a dual-manifest product with artifacts likely pushes the same slot twice and hits E286 (inferred from code, not reproduced).
One matching non-yanked file yields Exact, so a partial Python upload is adopted as complete.
The roster check requires each operation's (package, version) to have a decision entry; an owner id absent from a partial selection would fail with E285.
The tag name is rendered from package.id rather than the identity, so duplicate tag ops for dual packages have identical payloads.
redact_known_secrets can only remove known patterns; the brief's `redact_native_output` helper does not exist.

friction: Stack PR #205 conflicted with main after #202 edited a test inside the block being moved out of init.rs.
The assistant wrongly told the user #210 was still waiting on checks when it had already been merged.
The first #230 design shipped with serious performance and correctness flaws that only the independent review exposed.
GitHub timed out on `gh release list` and `git fetch`, so the 0.10.3 tags could not be confirmed at one point.
The sandbox refused an `xargs` form, forcing Python rewrite scripts.
The first negative control tripped an unrelated repository-mismatch guard and proved nothing.
The earlier recommendation on W3 decision 1 overlooked the T09 'envelope binding' text.
Agent reports were truncated and needed follow-up requests.
open_items: User decisions pending: W3 decisions 1-3 (build inside `execute` vs manifest, name-only rerun, ignore extras), the derived-owner option, and whether to build W10b (leaning defer).
Reproduce E286 and run `--package` on a dual package before committing to the shared-effects collapse.
#230 needs re-review after the redesign; lighter edge cases remain (bare-tag-to-blob E051 noise was addressed, but unpromoted-package qualified-tag adoption is a policy question).
SYS-BARRIER (#213) should merge after the 0.10.3 publish and will roll into the next release PR.
W1 CI credential check: write the job, name the platform asset, and define behavior when no suitable release exists. Codex noted fork PRs do get a read-only token.
W4: inventory all provider stdout/stderr leak paths beyond receipts before adopting a closed details enum.
W0 branch deletion needs per-branch user confirmation; the local plan's W4 brief should be corrected for the missing helper.
Hand-made lightweight tag at HEAD for a finished release fails with E167 until the next commit.
PyPI confirmation retry window should be extended to minutes; twine mid-list failure, private index behavior and the 14-day rule remain unverified.
W8 (SYS-MATURIN) and W9 (SYS-OWNER, SYS-DEMOTION) remain gated on the D01 owner-contract decision.
